findings.reason: the author would either relocate the runner to the core process/cache module or state why velocity is an acceptable home for git access but not for cache paths, resolving an inconsistency between §13's two placement decisions that a reader cannot currently resolve from the text.
findings.text: §13 places the package's core git process runner on `reckon/velocity.py`, a velocity-report module, while §13 argues at length that the cache-path cascade must live in its own core module precisely because "five unrelated consumers ... should not import a velocity report to find a cache directory"; the runner's consumer set is larger — the git-access followup will route the 21 modules and 63 direct invocations through it — so the same principle that built the cache module is left unaddressed for git, and §13's design concentrates the runner, the tree lister, the sources reader, `read_blobs`, `git`, `_is_ancestor` and `_blob_sha` on one feature module

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the cache cascade is correctly given one deep module (`cache_root(kind)` hiding a five-row ordering table), but the git process runner is parked on the velocity report module rather than a core process module, the asymmetry the plan's own cache rationale rules out.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan is itself a de-duplication; it names the owner it retires or delegates to for every fork (`pick_input_cache_root` retired, `velocity_cache_root` delegates, the detector's `_git`/`_cache_root` retired onto §13's owners), and I found no shared mechanism it forks instead of extending. `_store._config_home` is not a cache-path owner and does not read `XDG_CACHE_HOME`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §12 states its net is zero (public sources reader added, public `revised_python` retired) and §13 states its net is one (process runner + `cache_root` added, public `pick_input_cache_root` retired), each accounting in its own text, so neither section adds surface without naming what it retires.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase and cites by name the mechanisms it extends, wraps or declines (`velocity.git`, `read_blobs`, `interface_counts.read_trees`, `_plan_documents`, `routing._git`, `service._run`, the detector's `_git`/`revised_python`/`_cache_root`, and five named cache cascades), each verified to exist at the stated lines.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every retained wrapper states its reason: `velocity.git` keeps its name so "its four decoding callers are untouched"; `routing._git` stays as "error-domain translation and not a second runner"; `service._run` is named and declined for the layering inversion. None is a wrapper with no stated justification.
